subject: RM_Ashwallow

reply.subject: RM_Ashwallow

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a low, broad, armoured dome covered in large pale ash-grey plates with darker cracked edges, over a darker slate-grey hide that has small oval scutes. South: a symmetrical dome. A small, narrow plated head sits low at the front centre with two small dark eyes and a short fringe of pale peg teeth along the jaw. Plated rounded lumps on both sides read as tucked forelimbs. East: a long, low oval dome in profile. A small head pokes out at the right, tapering to a narrow snout with an eye and a row of peg teeth underneath. Plated lumps along the lower flank read as folded legs. North: a dome seen from behind, with no head or eyes. Plates run over the top, small oval scutes are on the lower back, and two rounded plated haunches sit at the bottom corners. The facings are a similar size.
observed.south.png: Full-res south. Front view of the dome, with the head tucked low in the centre. The head is narrower than a hand's width relative to the body and tapers slightly downward. It has small dark eyes and about 8–9 blunt pale teeth hanging below the jaw line. Plated limb pads flank the head. Painterly shading, a soft dark outline, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Full-res east. Side profile of an elongated dome with overlapping cracked plates. The head at the right is small and wedge-shaped, tapering to a pointed snout like a pangolin or armadillo, with a few small teeth beneath. No legs are visible as legs, only plated bulges low on the flank. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Full-res north. The rear of the dome: plates on top, a band of small oval scutes, two rounded haunch lumps and a dark cleft between them at the bottom centre. No face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature spans about 2 cells wide and about 0.8 cells tall beside the vanilla human. It is lower than the human's head and about twice the human's width. At 32 px/cell it reads as a pale grey mound with a darker base, much bigger than the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head and face toward the camera, with eyes and teeth at front centre.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back plates, haunches and rear cleft. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are angled side-on views of a dome. None is overhead.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Measured height spread is 6%. Visually consistent in the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Same plate palette, scute pattern, limb pads and teeth on every facing. The head is present on south and east and absent on north as expected.

SIGNATURE.seen: The defining tucked, smooth ash-grey dome with cracked plates is clearly legible on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: The small tapered wedge head with overlapping plates over a rounded body reads as a pangolin or armadillo curled up. The plate shapes add some tortoise feel. It is little beyond an Earth armoured mammal.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 legs folded flat along sides: present, as plated pads tucked against the flanks with no pillar legs. 2 low broad dome: present. 3 wide, flat spade face: ABSENT. The head is narrow and tapers to a pointed snout in east, and is small and narrow in south, not a broad flat spade wider than it is tall. 4 row of blunt raking teeth: present, as a visible fringe of pale blunt pegs on south and east (small but legible). 5 cracked grey shoulder plates: present, with plates over the shoulders and the whole back.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, soft-shaded, a believable texture, small dull eyes. Not cartoon, cel or photo.

OURS.seen: A bespoke ashwallow design. Not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Clean cut-out on every facing. No ground patch, ash pile or shadow.

SCALE.seen: About 2 cells wide and low beside the human. That fits a 'low, broad grazer' at drawSize 1.9.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a distinct pale plated mound against the ground. The head is barely visible, but the silhouette is clear.

findings.seen: The head is small and narrow. In profile it tapers to a pointed pangolin-like snout, and from the front it is narrower than either limb pad.
findings.quote: face is wide and flat as a spade, with no rounded muzzle, nostril bulb or hippo snout
findings.fix: The head is a broad, flat spade-shaped shovel nearly as wide as the front of the dome, thin in profile with a straight blunt leading edge, its blunt raking teeth lining that whole wide front edge.

findings.seen: A curled armoured body with a small wedge head reads as a pangolin or armadillo tucked into a ball.
findings.quote: Invented creatures and plants read as ALIEN, never as a recoloured Earth species.
findings.fix: The ashwallow reads as alien through a very wide flat spade face fused into the dome rim, and plates that join into a continuous smooth ash-grey shell with crack lines rather than overlapping pangolin scales.

findings.seen: Every facing shows the animal fully tucked into its fire-shelter dome. There is no active grazing posture, so in game the walking or grazing animal will always look like a closed dome.
findings.quote: It works the quickgrass in the calm between burns ... drops flat, digs in, curls its legs under, and goes still.
findings.fix: The body sprite shows the grazing posture: low and broad with the short legs splayed out to the sides and the spade face down at the ground, while the plates still suggest how it would close into a dome.

findings.seen: The raking teeth are a short fringe of small pegs dangling below a narrow jaw. They are legible at max zoom but vanish at 32 px.
findings.quote: jaw edge lined with a visible row of blunt raking digging teeth, not tusks
findings.fix: A bold row of blunt, squared digging teeth runs along the full width of the spade-shaped jaw edge, clearly visible on south and east.

findings.seen: At 32 px the head and teeth disappear and the creature reads as a plain grey rock mound.
findings.quote: legibility at 32 px. Both are polish.
findings.fix: The wide flat face shows as a dark distinct band at the front of the dome so the animal reads as a creature, not a rock, at 32 px per cell.

reply.needs_call_why: The dome, plates, folded legs and teeth are all there and well painted, but the spade face departure is clearly missing (narrow pangolin snout), and the whole thing leans pangolin/armadillo. A second reviewer should weigh whether that is blocking. They should also decide whether the always-tucked pose is acceptable for the default body sprite.
proposals: Clarify whether a creature whose description has a resting/defensive pose (dome, curl) should have its body sprite in the active pose or the defensive pose. The card has no checklist item for it.

request.subject: RM_Ashwallow

edits.change: The head is a broad, flat spade-shaped shovel nearly as wide as the front of the body, thin in profile with a straight blunt leading edge, fused into the front rim of the body.
A bold row of blunt, squared digging teeth runs along the full width of the spade-shaped jaw edge, each tooth large enough to read at 32 px, clearly visible in front and side views.

The hide plates join into a continuous, smooth ash-grey shell divided by fine crack lines, flowing from the shoulders over the back; the wide flat spade face merges into the shell rim, giving an alien silhouette unlike any armoured Earth animal.

The ashwallow is shown in its grazing posture: body low and broad, short legs splayed out to the sides, spade face lowered to the ground raking the root-mat. The shell plates and low rounded back suggest how it would close into a dome.

invariants: transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
low, broad body close to the ground
cracked plate pattern heaviest across the shoulders, thinning toward the hindquarters with darker grey skin showing between plates
small eyes at the sides of the face
rear view shows the back and haunches with eyes hidden
request.prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite on a transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline. The ashwallow is a low, broad grazer of a burning savanna, shown in its grazing posture: the body sits close to the ground, wide and rounded across the back, with four short legs splayed outward to the sides and the head lowered so the face rests at ground level raking the root-mat. The head is a broad, flat spade-shaped shovel nearly as wide as the front of the body, thin in profile with a straight blunt leading edge, fused into the front rim of the body. A bold row of blunt, squared digging teeth runs along the full width of that spade-shaped jaw edge, each tooth large enough to stay readable at 32 px, clearly visible in front and side views. Small eyes sit at the sides of the face. The hide is a cool, pale, spent-ash grey. Cracked plates of hide are heaviest across the shoulders and join into a continuous, smooth ash-grey shell divided by fine crack lines, flowing over the back; toward the hindquarters the plates thin out and darker grey skin shows between them. The low rounded shell and short folding legs suggest how the body would close into a smooth dome. The rear view, seen from behind, shows the back, shell and haunches with the eyes hidden. Build the body from this description alone, reference: none.
